title: Conceptual viable price window
description: A scenario concept showing the space between producer viability requirements and the consumer affordability ceiling.
plainLanguageSummary: A stable market window exists only when consumers can sustainably pay enough to support ongoing production and replacement investment. The boundaries are illustrative, not observed global prices.
sourceNotes: Interpretive framing informed by Gail Tverberg, Our Finite World (2015)
Illustrative normalized values are a conceptual visualization, not a global breakeven estimate.

methodology.formula: Producer viability floor and consumer affordability ceiling are normalized illustrative boundaries on a 0-100 scale.
limitations: Requirements vary by geology, decline rates, financing, taxation, transport, refining configuration, and company balance sheets.
No single global producer floor or consumer ceiling is estimated here.

states.label: Viable range
states.interpretation: The affordability ceiling remains above the producer viability floor, leaving a conceptual operating range.

states.label: Affordability squeeze
states.interpretation: The two boundaries converge; consumers feel pressure while producers still require investment-supporting prices.

states.label: No stable price window
states.interpretation: Producer requirements exceed what consumers can sustainably pay, so contraction can push benchmark prices lower while future supply becomes more vulnerable.
